statement: The equation $x^{3}-x-1=0$ has a root $\alpha$ near $1.3$. Show that the iteration $x_{n+1}=\sqrt[3]{x_{n}+1}$ converges to $\alpha$, and carry out two iterations starting from $x_{0}=1.3$.
solution: The rearrangement $x=\sqrt[3]{x+1}$ has $g(x)=\sqrt[3]{x+1}$ with $g'(x)=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{-2/3}$. Near $x=1.3$, $|g'(x)|\approx\frac{1}{3}(2.3)^{-2/3}\approx0.19<1$, so the iteration converges. Two iterations: $x_{1}=\sqrt[3]{2.3}\approx1.3200$ and $x_{2}=\sqrt[3]{2.3200}\approx1.3238$.
